exercises.title: Modal Verbs — Recupera
exercises.description: Ricostruisci significato e forma di can, must, have to e should.
exercises.instructions: Decidi prima se stai parlando di capacità, obbligo, divieto, scelta o consiglio.

sections.title: Recupera
sections.instructions: Decidi prima se stai parlando di capacità, obbligo, divieto, scelta o consiglio.

questions.title: Modal verbs: scegli dal significato
questions.prompt: Prima di esercitarti
questions.instructions: Leggi le regole e osserva gli esempi.
questions.learning_objective: Choose and form basic modal structures from communicative meaning.

content.body: I modali non sono intercambiabili: la forma corretta dipende da ciò che vuoi comunicare — capacità, regola, divieto, opzione o consiglio.
content.intro: Per uno studente italiano il contrasto decisivo è spesso mustn't / don't have to. Prima chiediti se una cosa è vietata o semplicemente facoltativa.

sections.title: Can: capacità, permesso e possibilità semplice
sections.body: Can + verbo base esprime soprattutto ciò che una persona sa/può fare, un permesso semplice o una possibilità generale. Nelle domande can va prima del soggetto.

examples.text: It can get very cold here in winter.

sections.title: Can, must, should + verbo base
sections.body: Dopo can, must e should usa direttamente la forma base: niente to e niente -s.

sections.title: Must e have to: obbligo
sections.body: Entrambi esprimono obbligo. A questo livello usa must per un obbligo forte o dato direttamente dal parlante; have to per una regola o necessità esterna. Nella terza persona: has to.

correct.text: You must be quiet now. · Marta has to wear a uniform at work.

incorrect.text: Marta have to wear a uniform.

sections.title: Mustn't ≠ don't have to
sections.body: Mustn't significa 'è vietato'. Don't have to significa 'non è necessario': puoi farlo se vuoi.

correct.text: You mustn't park here. · You don't have to bring food; lunch is provided.

incorrect.text: You mustn't bring food. (= non è necessario)

sections.title: Should: consiglio
sections.body: Should/shouldn't dà un consiglio: è una buona o cattiva idea, non una regola obbligatoria.

examples.text: You should revise a little every day.
You shouldn't stay up all night before the exam.

sections.title: Have to segue il Present Simple
sections.body: Have to non si comporta esattamente come can/must/should: usa has to con he/she/it e do/does nelle domande e negative.
sections.pattern: I/you/we/they have to · he/she/it has to · don't/doesn't have to · Do/Does ... have to?

sections.title: Prima di continuare
points: Have to: obbligo/necessità esterna; don't have to: non necessario.
Have to usa has/do/does come un verbo al Present Simple.

questions.title: Una capacità
questions.prompt: Nina speaks English and Spanish, but she does not know Japanese. Which sentence is true?
questions.learning_objective: Use can + base verb for ability

options.text: Nina can speak Spanish.
Nina cans speak Spanish.
Nina can to speak Spanish.

feedback.explanation: Can non prende -s e non prende to: can speak.

questions.title: Chiedere permesso
questions.prompt: Which question is appropriate?
questions.instructions: Leggi il dialogo e scegli la risposta più naturale.
questions.learning_objective: Use can in a basic permission question

content.scenario: A student wants to leave class for two minutes.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Excuse me, I need some water.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Of course. What do you need?

options.text: Can I go and get some water?
Do I can go and get some water?
Can I to go and get some water?

feedback.explanation: Can va prima del soggetto: Can I go...?

questions.title: Una regola
questions.prompt: At this laboratory, safety glasses are compulsory for everyone. You ___.
questions.learning_objective: Choose have to for a clear external requirement

options.text: have to wear safety glasses
should wear safety glasses if you want
don't have to wear safety glasses

feedback.explanation: È una regola obbligatoria esterna: have to.

questions.title: Vietato o facoltativo?
questions.prompt: The sign says “NO PHONES DURING THE EXAM”. Students ___.
questions.learning_objective: Distinguish prohibition from absence of obligation

options.text: mustn't use their phones
don't have to use their phones
should use their phones

questions.title: Terza persona
questions.prompt: Completa.
questions.learning_objective: Use has to and does not have to with third-person singular meaning

content.text_template: Sara works at a hotel. She [[blank_1]] start at 7 a.m. on Mondays, but she [[blank_2]] wear a jacket; the uniform is optional.

feedback.explanation: She has to...; nella negativa: she doesn't have to...

questions.title: Un consiglio
questions.prompt: Dovresti dormire di più prima degli esami.
questions.learning_objective: Produce should + base verb for advice

accepted_answers: You should sleep more before exams.
You should get more sleep before exams.
You should sleep more before the exams.

feedback.explanation: Should dà un consiglio e prende il verbo base.

questions.title: Preparare una gita
questions.prompt: What can Maya say?
questions.instructions: Leggi il dialogo e scegli la risposta più naturale.
questions.learning_objective: Use do not have to when something is unnecessary but not prohibited

content.scenario: Two students are reading the school trip information.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Lunch is included in the price.

turns.speaker: Luca
turns.text: Great. I was going to make sandwiches.

options.text: You don't have to bring lunch.
You mustn't bring lunch.
You should not to bring lunch.

feedback.explanation: Lunch è incluso: portarlo non è necessario, non vietato.

questions.title: Una forma da correggere
questions.prompt: Correggi: My brother can to drive, but he doesn’t have a car.
questions.learning_objective: Remove to after can while preserving the sentence meaning

accepted_answers: My brother can drive, but he doesn't have a car.
My brother can drive, but he does not have a car.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish required action from prohibited action in rules

content.text_template: Members [[blank_1]] return weights after use. Children under 14 [[blank_2]] enter the weights area alone.

questions.title: Facoltativo
questions.prompt: Non devi portare un computer: puoi usare quelli della scuola.
questions.learning_objective: Produce absence of obligation and can permission/availability in one context

accepted_answers: You don't have to bring a computer; you can use the school's computers.
You do not have to bring a computer; you can use the school computers.
You don't have to bring a laptop; you can use the school's computers.
You do not have to bring a laptop; you can use the school computers.

feedback.explanation: Don't have to = non è necessario; can = possibilità disponibile.

questions.title: Prima di un esame
questions.prompt: A friend has an exam tomorrow and has studied for six hours without a break. What is the best advice?
questions.learning_objective: Choose should for non-compulsory advice from context

options.text: You should take a short break.
You must take a break because it is illegal not to.
You don't have to take any breaks ever.

feedback.explanation: È un consiglio, non una regola.

questions.title: Un turno di lavoro
questions.prompt: Leggi il contesto.
questions.learning_objective: Integrate third-person obligation and absence of obligation from workplace context

content.text_template: Paolo works at reception. On Fridays he [[blank_1]] stay until 9 p.m. because the hotel closes late, but he [[blank_2]] wear a tie; the manager says a plain shirt is fine.

feedback.explanation: Paolo = he: has to; opzionale = doesn't have to.
